fix(app): give macOS back its dock margin — the icon shipped a fifth too big

TRA-780 took the artwork's padding out on the reasoning that our plate rendered
smaller than its neighbours'. That was backwards. macOS draws every dock icon in
the same slot, and a conforming icon leaves margin inside its own canvas rather
than filling it — Apple's grid puts the rounded square at 824 of 1024, 80.5%.

Measured off a real dock screenshot, every neighbour's plate is 94px and ours
shipped at 116 — 23% larger, which is what Nikolai spotted.

The margin goes into the rasteriser rather than back into the master, because it
is a packaging convention for one platform and not part of the mark: the lockups
inline the same master and must not inherit a dock margin. The masters keep
drawing the plate edge to edge and their test still asserts that.

Rendered at the dock's 117px slot the plate is now 95px against the neighbours'
94. A new test measures the shipped icon-1024.png rather than the master, so the
two conventions cannot drift into each other again.

docs: the padded canvas rounds to 1273, not 1272

Math.round(1024 / (824/1024)) is 1273 and the inset 124.5; the comment claimed
1272/124. The rendered plate was always the intended 824px — only the note was
wrong. Caught in review.
